levelGuides.A1: Speak slowly, with a pause after every sentence. Present tense only, sentences under 8 words, everyday words, no idioms. Address me as Sie. Repeat a question in the same words before you simplify it.
levelGuides.A2: Speak slowly and clearly. Present and Perfekt, simple weil / dass clauses, everyday vocabulary. Address me as du unless the roleplay says otherwise.
levelGuides.B1: Speak at a calm natural pace. Everyday and work vocabulary, subordinate clauses are fine, avoid rare idioms. Address me as du unless the roleplay says otherwise.
levelGuides.B2: Speak at natural pace with natural idioms. Take a real position and defend it so I have something to argue against. Register as the topic requires.
levelGuides.C1: Speak at full natural pace, with idioms, abstract vocabulary and long sentences. Challenge my claims and ask for precision.
levelGuides.C2: Speak as you would to an educated native speaker: full pace, irony, allusion, register shifts. Push back hard on vague or generic answers.

turnLengths.A1: Keep your own turns to one short sentence plus the question, so I do most of the talking.
turnLengths.A2: Keep your own turns to 1-2 sentences, so I do most of the talking.
turnLengths.B1: Keep your own turns to 1-2 sentences, so I do most of the talking.
turnLengths.B2: Your turns may be 2-4 sentences when you make a counter-argument; I should still speak more than you.
turnLengths.C1: Your turns may be 3-4 sentences when you make a counter-argument; I should still speak more than you.
turnLengths.C2: Your turns may be a full argument of 3-5 sentences; I should still speak more than you.
